# EDN Core Behavioral Specification

## 1. Purpose

The EDN core module distributes entropy to a set of hardware endpoint ports. It accepts CSRNG commands either from software or from an internal automatic request flow, sends those commands on a CSRNG application command interface, receives 128-bit entropy words in response, and delivers that entropy to endpoints as 32-bit words.

The module behaves as an entropy distribution point only. It does not generate entropy and it does not modify the entropy data. It only performs command sequencing, data width conversion, endpoint arbitration, and error/status reporting.

## 2. Interfaces

The module provides the following externally observable interfaces:

- A clock and reset interface.
- A register interface for software control and status.
- One CSRNG application command/response interface.
- A parameterized number of endpoint interfaces, defaulting to four, each with a 32-bit data path.

The CSRNG application interface carries:

- CSRNG command words, 32 bits each.
- Command completion status.
- Entropy words, 128 bits each.
- A FIPS indication associated with each entropy word.

Each endpoint interface carries:

- A request signal from the endpoint.
- An acknowledge signal from the module.
- A 32-bit data bus from the module.
- A FIPS indication associated with the delivered data.

## 3. Reset and Initialization

After reset:

- The module shall be in a disabled state.
- No CSRNG command shall be issued.
- No endpoint transfer shall be acknowledged. Data bus values outside a transfer do not constitute delivered entropy.
- All internal queues and data storage shall be cleared.
- All interrupt and alert outputs shall be inactive.

The module shall remain inactive until software enables it through the register interface. Normal operation begins only when the enable field is programmed to its true multi-bit value.

## 4. General Behavior

### 4.1 CSRNG Command Handling

The module treats CSRNG command words as opaque. It shall not parse, validate, alter, or reorder the fields of a command word.

The module shall present commands on the CSRNG application interface one at a time. A new command may be presented only when the previous command has completed or been accepted according to the interface handshake.

The module shall not generate commands spontaneously except when one of the following operation modes is active:

- Software command mode.
- Boot-time request mode.
- Auto request mode.

### 4.2 Entropy Data Reception

The module shall accept 128-bit entropy words from the CSRNG application interface when its internal storage is ready.

If internal storage is full, the module shall stop accepting further entropy words and apply backpressure on the interface.

When an entropy word is accepted, the module shall also capture its FIPS indication.

### 4.3 Data Distribution to Endpoints

Each accepted 128-bit entropy word shall be made available to endpoint ports as four 32-bit words.

Each 128-bit word is allocated as a whole to one requesting endpoint whose local packer is empty. That endpoint then receives the four 32-bit portions in sequence. Different endpoints have separate local packers and acknowledgement state machines.

Endpoint data transfer behavior:

- When an endpoint requests data and a 32-bit word is available, the module shall assert its endpoint acknowledge signal and present the data on the endpoint data bus.
- The data word shall be considered consumed when the endpoint request and the module acknowledge are both asserted in the same cycle.
- The module shall not assert acknowledge for an endpoint unless a data word is available for that endpoint.
- The data bus shall remain stable after a word is presented until the next endpoint transfer begins.
- If no data word is available, the module shall not acknowledge a request.

An arbiter allocates one incoming 128-bit block at a time among requesting empty endpoint packers. Endpoints with buffered data may acknowledge independently. Pending requests can progress when entropy continues to arrive and the module remains enabled without a fatal fault.

### 4.4 Endpoint FIPS Indication

The module shall provide a FIPS output on every endpoint interface.

This output shall indicate whether the entropy currently being delivered to that endpoint was produced by the CSRNG with full FIPS-approved processing.

The FIPS indication shall be stable while data from the same entropy word is being delivered. It shall only change when data from a different entropy word begins to be delivered to that endpoint.

## 5. Operation Modes

### 5.1 Software Command Mode

In software command mode, firmware issues CSRNG commands one at a time through the command request register.

The module shall accept a software command only when the command interface is ready. The ready status shall be visible in the command status register.

When a software command is written:

- The module shall queue the command and send it on the CSRNG application interface.
- While the command is outstanding, the software command interface shall not be ready to accept another command.
- When the CSRNG application interface returns completion for that command, the module shall record the completion status and generate the command-request-done interrupt event.
- The completion status shall be visible in the command status register.

Software must obey the command-ready indication when writing command words. The core filters writes by its operating mode; it does not generally gate each write with cmd_rdy.

### 5.2 Boot-Time Request Mode

When boot-time request mode is enabled, the module shall automatically generate a CSRNG command sequence without further software command writes.

The boot sequence sends the configured boot instantiate command, waits for its acknowledgement, sends one configured boot generate command, and waits for its acknowledgement. It then enters a boot-done state and issues no further boot commands until the module is disabled and enabled again.

Boot-time request mode shall take precedence if both boot-time request mode and auto request mode are enabled.

The software command status interface is not used to report completions of boot-time commands. The module shall not generate the command-request-done interrupt for boot-time command completions.

### 5.3 Auto Request Mode

In auto request mode, the module automatically alternates between generate commands and reseed commands from two software-loadable command queues.

Before entering auto request mode, software is expected to:

- Issue an instantiate command through the software command interface.
- Load the generate command queue.
- Load the reseed command queue.
- Program a nonzero maximum number of generate commands between reseeds when generate requests are desired. Leaving the register unwritten retains its defined reset value of zero.

When auto request mode is active, the module shall:

- Issue generate commands from the generate command queue.
- Decrement the remaining-generate count when the last word of a queued generate command is sent to the output command queue.
- When the configured maximum number of generate commands has been reached, issue a reseed command from the reseed command queue.
- Reload the count from the current maximum-request register when the last reseed-command word is sent, and wait for acknowledgement before the next dispatch.

The maximum-request register resets to zero. At automatic dispatch, zero remaining requests selects a reseed and a nonzero count selects a generate. Without a maximum-register write, the first automatic command after the initial software command acknowledgement is a reseed; a zero reload continues selecting reseeds. A software write immediately loads the count, and exiting automatic operation reloads it. The module repeats automatic dispatch until mode or enable is deasserted.

While auto request mode is active, after the initial instantiate command has completed, writes to the software command request register shall have no effect on the automatic sequence.

### 5.4 Command Queues

The module provides two command queues:

- A generate command queue.
- A reseed command queue.

Each queue shall be capable of holding up to 13 command words.

Software loads a queue by writing command words to the associated command register. Each write appends one word to the queue.

If software attempts to write to a queue that is already full, the write shall not be accepted, and a fatal error shall be reported.

A command queue reset function is provided in the control register. When set to true, both command queues shall be cleared.

Software shall return the queue reset field to its false state before loading new commands. While the reset field is true, command writes shall not be accepted.

## 6. Register-Visible Status and Control

The module shall make the following behavior visible through the register interface:

- Control fields for enabling the module, selecting operation modes, and resetting command queues.
- Command words for software-issued commands, boot-time commands, generate queue loading, and reseed queue loading.
- The maximum number of generate requests between reseed requests.
- Software command ready and completion status.
- Interrupt state and enable status.
- Recoverable alert status.
- Fatal error code status.
- A debug observation status for the main operational state machine.

The debug state observation field shall reflect the current state of the primary operational control flow. It is read-only and shall not affect behavior.

## 7. Interrupts

The module shall provide two interrupt outputs:

### 7.1 Command Request Done Interrupt

This interrupt shall be generated when a software-initiated CSRNG command completes.

The interrupt event shall be reported through the interrupt status and enable mechanism. If the interrupt is enabled, the interrupt output shall be asserted.

This interrupt shall not be generated for commands issued automatically by boot-time request mode or auto request mode.

### 7.2 Fatal Error Interrupt

This interrupt shall be generated when a fatal error condition is detected.

Fatal error conditions include:

- Command queue overflow, underflow, or inconsistent queue state.
- Output command queue overflow, underflow, or inconsistent state.
- An illegal state in any internal operational state machine.
- An integrity error in the generate request counter.

The fatal error interrupt shall be reported through the interrupt status and enable mechanism. If enabled, the interrupt output shall be asserted.

## 8. Alerts

### 8.1 Fatal Alert

The module shall assert the fatal alert output when any fatal error condition occurs.

Fatal alert conditions are the same as those listed for the fatal error interrupt.

The fatal alert shall be accompanied by error code status bits identifying the source of the error.

### 8.2 Recoverable Alert

The module shall assert the recoverable alert output when it detects that the low 64 bits of two consecutive 128-bit entropy words delivered toward the endpoint data path are identical.

This condition is treated as a possible data integrity failure and shall also be recorded in the recoverable alert status register.

The recoverable alert output shall be asserted as an event pulse when the repeated data pattern is detected.

### 8.3 Invalid Control Field Encodings

The module shall validate the multi-bit encoded control fields used for enabling and mode selection.

If a control field is programmed to an illegal or invalid encoding, the module shall record the corresponding recoverable alert status bit. This condition shall not, by itself, cause a fatal alert.

### 8.4 Diagnostic Event Forcing

The register interface shall allow software to force interrupt or alert events for diagnostic purposes.

Writing the appropriate diagnostic register field shall cause the corresponding interrupt or alert output to behave as if a real event had occurred.

## 9. Error Reporting

### 9.1 Error Code Status

The module shall provide error code status bits for:

- Reseed command queue errors.
- Generate command queue errors.
- Output command queue errors.
- Endpoint acknowledge state machine errors.
- Main operational state machine errors.
- Counter integrity errors.
- Queue write errors.
- Queue read errors.
- Queue state errors.

The queue write, read, and state error bits shall classify the type of failure detected in any of the command or output queues.

Fatal error status bits shall remain set until reset.

### 9.2 Queue Error Details

For each queue, the module shall detect and report:

- A write attempt when the queue is full.
- A read attempt when the queue is empty.
- A condition where the queue reports both full and empty at the same time.

These queue conditions report fatal errors while EDN is enabled. Counter and state-machine structural errors remain active independently of the functional enable.

### 9.3 State Machine Error Details

The module shall detect if any internal operational state machine enters an illegal or invalid state.

An illegal state condition shall be treated as a fatal error and shall be reported in the error code status register.

### 9.4 Counter Error Details

The module shall detect integrity failures in the counter used to limit the number of generate commands between reseed commands.

A counter integrity failure shall be treated as a fatal error.

## 10. Security Requirements

The module shall implement the following security-relevant behaviors:

- Multi-bit control fields shall be checked for valid encodings.
- Internal operational state machines shall be checked for illegal states.
- The generate request counter shall be protected against integrity failures.
- Entropy data shall be checked for repeated consecutive values.
- Commands shall not be accepted into full queues.
- Entropy data shall not be lost due to endpoint backpressure; if storage is full, the module shall stop accepting new data from the CSRNG application interface.

## 11. Summary of Functional Requirements

- The module shall be disabled after reset and shall not issue commands or distribute data until enabled.
- The module shall forward CSRNG command words without modification.
- The module shall support software command mode, boot-time request mode, and auto request mode.
- The module shall convert 128-bit entropy words into 32-bit endpoint words.
- The module shall acknowledge endpoint requests only when data is available.
- The module shall preserve and forward the FIPS indication associated with entropy data.
- The module shall report command completion only for software-initiated commands.
- The module shall detect and report fatal queue, state machine, and counter errors.
- The module shall detect and report repeated entropy data as a recoverable alert.
- The module shall provide interrupt and alert outputs that reflect the corresponding detected events.

Reset is active-low and asynchronous to clk_i. All MuBi controls activate their function only for canonical true; noncanonical enable/mode/FIFO-reset values set their corresponding recoverable status bits. The repeated-data detector compares consecutive 128-bit block handoffs to endpoint packers using their low 64 bits, and the recoverable output pulses on the rising edge of this comparison condition. FIFO command words circulate back into their queue during automatic operation so a queued command can be reused. A FIFO-reset true value clears both command queues. Disabling EDN clears outgoing commands and suppresses endpoint acknowledgements; structural escalation takes priority over disable and holds error states until reset.
